findings: Original hash_video compiled unchanged; controlled FrameSource and frame-hash callback replace decoding deliberately. No ffmpeg or real video decoding validated.
Majority aggregation ignores failed empty frame hashes; every bit uses strict majority of valid frames, even ties become zero. Independent counts match 128 cases.
Frame order is discarded: all 128 reversed sequences produce identical aggregate hashes. Aggregate fingerprint cannot establish temporal equivalence.

Cleanup lambda is called explicitly, not by destructor: callback exception leaves temporary directory, confirmed with controlled failure. Only the test-owned directory was removed afterwards. Extraction exception also bypasses cleanup by source inspection.
Temporary directory identity uses basename plus process ID; concurrent same-basename inputs share directory and frame names. Source-only concurrency concern, no race experiment executed.

FrameSource probes duration and samples midpoint timestamps through one ffmpeg invocation per frame. Process statuses, finite duration and actual output freshness are not comprehensively validated; factory silently maps unknown strategies to evenly_spaced.

wHash applies separable full Haar transforms at a power-of-two image size at least twice requested grid and at least eight, extracts top-left coefficients, median excludes DC while output includes DC. This recipe must not be equated with other wHash implementations without oracle comparison.
remaining: Real video decoding, wavelet independent oracle, projection and full CLI qualification
